DevOps Factory
Intent-driven Operations for delivering Enterprise outcomes
Software Creation Outpaces Software Operations
The velocity of software production is higher than ever,
creating a paradox where code is written faster than it can be reliably and safely shipped.

2X
PR Volume
Al Coding Assistants:
have drastically accelerated the core software creation process.

Software Operations
AI-Accelerated Speed
1x
No Boost
Operations Stagnation:
The ops later has failed to scale or match development velocity spikes
Reliability Gap:
Creates a hazardous bottleneck where code is written faster than it can safely ship
Manual delivery creates a massive human toll and cost bottleneck
Supervised Execution:
Deployments require engineers to monitor pipelines for 45 minutes.
Stale Documentation:
Teams manage 200 runbooks, with only about 30 being current.
Deployment Paralysis:
Developers avoid shipping on Fridays due to untenable risk-to-reward ratios.
Approval Gridlock:
Deployment pipelines have grown to 14 manual approval steps deep.
Reactive SRE Fails to Solve the On-Call Crisis
Systemic bottlenecks and failure modes in modern incident response
Extended MTTR:
Average P1 incidents take 4 hours to resolve, with the first 90 minutes spent just agreeing on the broken component.
Burnout:
The chaos of incomplete context during on-call rotations is the leading cause of
engineer attrition.
Fragmented Archaeology:
Root Cause Analysis (RCA) is a
week-long project spanning six disconnected tools.
Blind Spots:
Most AI SRE tools lack visibility into the infrastructure changes and deployment
events that cause the majority of incidents.
Stateless Domain Agents Fail to Solve Cross-Domain Problems
The velocity of software production is higher than ever,
creating a paradox where code is written faster than it can be reliably and safely shipped.
The Domain Silos
Engineering teams have excellent tools, but these domains operate in absolute isolation.
CI/CD Pipelines
Deployment loops run automatically but lack infrastructure visibility
Infrastructure Automation
Provisioning runs in isolation,
producing undetected manual drift.
Observability Stack
Metrics track real-time health, detached from the system change history.
T-8 Mins
CI/CD Deploy
A deployment pipeline executes successfully, introducing silent infrastructure drift.
The Context Gap
Zero Shared History
Individual agents accelerate specific tasks but fail because they do not share operational history.
No bridge connects the state across domains.
T-0 Mins
P1 Incident
An SRE investigating a critical alert cannot automatically see the deployment that occurred prior.
Autonomous
DevOps Factory
Engineered autonomously from simple
declarative intent
“Simply Describe Your Outcomes, ADF Builds and Runs the Factory”
Plain-Language Intent
StackGen's Autonomous DevOps Factory ADF begins with plain-language intent. Engineering teams describe their desired operational outcomes.
Version-Controlled Spec
ADF then translates this intent into a version-controlled Factory Spec, assembling out-of-the-box and custom agents, defining SLOs, and establishing governance requirements to deliver those outcomes autonomously
Stateful Memory and Outcome Accountability Drive the Factory Model
Unlike individual agents that are stateless and assist within a single domain, a factory owns the full operations loop and is accountable for outcomes.
Full-Loop Accountability:
ADF connects operational domains, holding the entire loop accountable.
Stateful Memory:
Correlates immediate events and tracks long-term operational history, enabling multi-agent orchestration that improves over time without manual reconfiguration.
The Operational Context Graph (OCG)
The OCG connects all operational domains into a queryable graph, separating a factory from a collection of agents
Infrastructure Topology
Current state and relationships of resources
Change Attribution
IaC changes and timestamps.
Drift History
Divergence from desired state
Observability Correlations
Infrastructure states linked
to anomalies.
Incident Causality
Infrastructure patterns linked to incident classes.
OCG Shared Intel
Aiden for SRE
Autonomous Incident Investigation & Remediation
Aiden for SRE investigates and resolves production incidents by leveraging infrastructure root cause context from the OCG.

It handles infrastructure-correlated incidents autonomously—tracing root cause, generating fixes, and deploying them through validated pipelines.

For a team experiencing 2 P1s per month, ADF targets a 40% prevention rate and reduces MTTR from 4 hours to under 15 minutes for infrastructure-correlated cases.

Aiden OS
The Production-Grade Agentic Infrastructure Runtime Layer
Aiden OS ensures the factory is reliable for production environments.
TEMPORAL CORE
Workflow Orchestration
Orchestrates workflows with
durability, retries, and state
tracking.
FINANCIAL GOVERNANCE
Cost Governance
Tracks inference token spend and automatically shifts familiar workloads to cheaper, optimized models.
INTELLIGENT ROUTING
Model Routing
Selects the appropriate LLM based on task type and OCG
confidence dynamically.
NATS MESSAGING
Event Messaging
Individual agents accelerate specific tasks but fail because they do not share operational history.
OPEN POLICY AGENT
Policy Enforcement
Enforces policy at every action
boundary before execution.
The Four-Step ADF Lifecycle
From Intent to Automated Learning
STEP 01
Intent
State the operational problem in plain language. (e.g. "reduce SRE on-call time for infra incidents").
STEP 02
Factory Spec
ADF translates intent into a reviewable spec defining agents, OCG data, SLOs, and escalation boundaries.
STEP 03
Factory Runtime
Agents execute their configured tasks, escalating novel edge
cases to humans with full context.
STEP 04
Factory Learning
Every cycle writes incident patterns and remediation outcomes back to the OCG, improving the system automatically.
